title: Indian Shares Lifted as Oil Eases and RBI's Rupee Defence Kicks In
excerpt: The rupee jumped about 1% at Monday's open as the RBI's special dollar window for oil companies took effect and Brent slipped to $103 — though markets closed lower as crude stayed above $100 and foreign selling continued.
body:
• Indian equities opened higher on Monday after snapping their longest weekly losing run in 25 years — Nifty closed Friday at 22,520.45, with GIFT Nifty pointing to a positive start.
  • The RBI's weekend measures redirect oil companies' dollar purchases out of the spot market through a special window for Indian Oil, HPCL and BPCL, and tighten hedging rules; the rupee opened about 1% stronger, near 95.77 per dollar.
  • Brent crude fell 1.6% to about $103 a barrel on expectations of a Russia-Ukraine energy ceasefire, but remains above $100, capping sentiment.
  • Foreign investors have sold Indian stocks for 11 straight sessions; analysts call the rebound a relief rally, not yet a confirmed recovery.

A stronger open on two tailwinds

Indian shares were set for a firmer start to the week as two of the market's biggest headwinds eased at once. Brent crude fell 1.6 percent to $103 a barrel after President Trump said Russia and Ukraine had agreed to halt attacks on each other's energy facilities following a US diesel-supply deal with Moscow, according to Reuters. At home, the Reserve Bank of India's weekend currency measures took effect: from Monday, the central bank supplies dollars directly to the three state-run oil marketing companies — Indian Oil, Hindustan Petroleum and Bharat Petroleum — through a special window, removing one of the largest sources of dollar demand from the spot market, alongside tighter rules on currency hedging and forward buying.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=mD811UQDo90

The rupee responded immediately, opening roughly 1 percent stronger near 95.77 per dollar after closing Friday at 96.73, close to its record low of 96.96 set in May. The currency has still lost more than 7 percent this year.

Why traders are not calling a recovery yet

The benchmarks came into Monday having just snapped an eight-week losing streak — the longest weekly losing run in 25 years — with the Nifty up 0.4 percent and the Sensex 0.8 percent last week on upbeat financial-sector updates and TCS earnings that underscored AI revenue growth. But foreign portfolio investors have offloaded shares for 11 consecutive sessions, including 35.69 billion rupees on Friday, and oil above $100 keeps India's import bill and inflation outlook under pressure. By the close, the early optimism had faded: BusinessLine's market wrap recorded the Sensex down about 548 points as the oil spike and foreign outflows reasserted themselves.

"The recent rebound after an eight-week losing streak is encouraging, but not sufficient to confirm a sustained recovery — at this stage, it appears more like a relief rally."

— Pabitro Mukherjee, Bajaj Broking

What to watch this week

Three variables will steer the market: crude, where Brent holding above $100 limits any rally; the rupee, where traders expect the RBI's window to support the currency near term while Emkay and others caution that high oil prices, capital outflows and a weak external balance will keep depreciation pressure alive; and earnings, with HCLTech reporting Monday and the results season widening. For NRI investors, the RBI's intervention has made the exchange rate briefly more favourable for rupee purchases than for remittances — a reminder that in a managed defence, timing transfers around central-bank operations can matter as much as the headline rate.
